To: group:levy-longsight-noticeboard
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Counterfeit pills — please read, then share this (safety post)

I'm a nurse and I'm posting this as a safety post, not as gossip about any particular night. Neighbourhood Policing put a warning on this board on the 6th (it's still up there, please read it) about blue tablets being sold as diazepam or "Xanax". Some of them contain nitazenes — synthetic opioids that can be far stronger than heroin. People have needed hospital treatment as a result.

Signs to look for:
- extreme drowsiness, hard to wake
- pinpoint pupils (tiny black dots in the middle of the eye)
- slow or noisy breathing
- blue lips

What to do if someone with you becomes unwell:
1. Ring 999 straight away. Don't wait and see.
2. Do NOT put them to bed to sleep it off. If their breathing is slowing, they are not sleeping — they may be losing oxygen to the brain, and by the time you realise, it's already been too long. Hours later is far too late.
3. Stay with them, keep the packet if you can, and tell the crew what was taken if you know.
4. Don't worry about getting in trouble. Nobody is in trouble for calling an ambulance. The police have been clear that their priority is preserving life, and they are not interested in making examples of the person who rings.

Naloxone: free nasal naloxone spray kits from Brightpath, the drug and alcohol service on Stockport Road (next to the launderette). Anyone can ask, no names needed, no referral, no forms. They do a quick ten minute training so you know how to use it. Open Mon–Fri 10–4, Thursdays until 7. If you know anyone who might ever come across this stuff, please pass it on.

On slagging the kids off: honestly it helps nobody. A teenager who is scared of being shouted at, or of their parents finding out, will not ring for help when their mate is in trouble. That silence is the whole problem. Same goes for the friends who panic, put someone to bed to sleep it off, and then ring hours later — that's how this ends badly.

I had a chat with my own lad (14) over tea last night. Plenty of eye rolls, but he listened, and he asked me what pinpoint pupils meant, which was more than I expected. Please have that same conversation.

Two asks:
1. Parents: talk to your kids about this THIS week. Not after half term, not "when it feels right" — this week. Tell them the signs, and tell them you'd rather they rang you at 2am than sat on it.
2. Everyone: share this post, don't just like it. Copy it into other groups, send it to parents, put it on your fridge. A post only reaches the people who scroll past it.

No naming, no guessing, no speculation about anyone. Just share the warning and look after each other.
